title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

errors: The boxed operator is written something like 'cons-W°' / 'S-W°'. From context it must denote complementation; as transcribed it is ambiguous, and the reading is uncertain.
The informal notation mixes ∖ and −; there is no substantive mathematical error. The check of the four endpoint cases is consistent.

ideas.what: Encoding a constructible subset of an interval by a set of strata of a subdivision, with a canonical minimal ('purified') representative; Purif(M) → Cons(M) is a bijection.
ideas.modern_name: Minimal adapted stratification / cell decomposition of a definable subset of R (o-minimal dimension 1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is programmatically mentioned in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this combinatorics is not published there.

ideas.what: Classification of vertices (isolated, lacunary, evanescent, semi-evanescent, ∂*) and their exchange under complementation.
ideas.modern_name: Local types of a 1-dimensional constructible set at a point; complement duality

ideas.what: Complement of the shadow equals the shadow of the dual polygon, hence Cons(M) is closed under complement.
ideas.modern_name: Boolean closure of constructible / definable sets

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary bookkeeping for 1-dimensional constructible sets and complements; correct but routine. Possibly of interest only as documentation of Grothendieck's 1986 tame-topology workshop terminology (ombre, évanescent, semi-évanescent, purifié).
transcription_corrections: 'séc' / 'semi-isomorphes' should read 'sév' = 'semi-évanescents', as announced at the end of the previous page.
'Φ_ex' should read '𝔏_év' (évanescents); the line reads '𝔏*_év = 𝔏**_év = ∅'.
The symbol Φ is Grothendieck's script 𝔏 (polygone), consistent with the next page.
The note under 𝔏_év reads 'disparaît en dualité'. The crossed-out alternatives under 𝔏*_sév are '∂I ∖ ∂I∩δ𝔏*' (struck), corrected to '∂I ∖ ∂I∩δ𝔏'.
The final line plausibly reads 'En effet, on récupère 𝔏'.
